title: Singular and plural: forms and agreement
summary: Choose natural singular or plural forms and verb agreement with paired objects, school subjects, invariant nouns, collective nouns, police and people. Treat a total amount, distance or time period as one quantity when the meaning calls for it.
learningObjectives: Use plural verbs with clothing and objects that conventionally have plural forms, and use a pair of for one set.
Recognise singular -ics subject names and news, and count means, series and species without changing their form.
Use plural agreement with police and people while recognising that British English collective nouns can take singular or plural agreement.
Use singular verbs for time, money and distance when a single total is the subject.

explanation.heading: Things made of two parts
explanation.body: Words such as trousers, shorts, tights, spectacles, scissors and binoculars are grammatically plural when they name a single item. Use are, have or these with the plural noun. For one set, say a pair of scissors or a pair of trousers; pair is singular, so this pair is correct. Multiple sets take pairs. The expression a scissors is not standard.
explanation.example: Those hiking trousers are waterproof, but this pair is too small.

explanation.heading: Singular subjects ending in -s
explanation.body: An -s ending does not always mean that a noun is plural. Academic subjects such as physics, economics and gymnastics normally take a singular verb when referring to a field of study or a sport. News is an uncountable singular noun in ordinary use: the news is, not the news are. Remember that politics can have other meanings, so use the singular pattern here for the academic field.
explanation.example: Economics is offered as an evening course at the college.

explanation.heading: Same noun form for one or several
explanation.body: Means, series and species have the same shape in the singular and plural. Use a or one to identify one item, and several, two or many for multiple items. The determiner and the context—not an extra -s—tell us the number: one species and several species. Agreement follows the actual number, not the ending alone.
explanation.example: Three documentary series are available, but only one series is new.

explanation.heading: Groups of people and plural-only people nouns
explanation.body: In British English, a collective noun such as team, committee, staff or family may take a singular verb when treated as one unit or a plural verb when the members are emphasised. Both patterns are sometimes possible, so context and consistent reference matter. Police and people, however, normally take plural verbs: the police are and several people have. For one officer, use a police officer, not a police.
explanation.example: The committee are discussing their different proposals before the vote.

explanation.heading: One sum, period or distance
explanation.body: Although a total may contain a plural measurement word, use a singular verb when you view it as one amount, period or distance. This is especially natural in judgements such as five hours is enough, or twenty kilometres is a long way. If separate coins, hours or distances are meant rather than one quantity, the meaning and agreement may change.
explanation.example: Eighty pounds is more than we planned to spend on the repair.

comparisons.title: One paired item versus one pair

left.label: Plural object noun
left.example: My headphones are in the drawer.
left.note: Headphones is grammatically plural even for one set.

right.label: Singular pair
right.example: This pair of headphones is brand-new.
right.note: The head noun pair controls the singular verb.

comparisons.title: A group name versus the police

left.label: Collective noun
left.example: The research team is meeting today.
left.note: Treating the team as a single group makes singular agreement natural.

right.label: Plural-only group noun
right.example: The police are speaking to witnesses.
right.note: Police takes plural agreement in standard usage.

examples.sentence: Her new binoculars have adjustable lenses.
examples.note: A plural-only object takes have even when it is one device.

examples.sentence: The news from the interview is positive.
examples.note: News is singular despite its -s ending.

examples.sentence: Several species of butterfly live in the reserve.
examples.note: Species has the same form for one and for several.

examples.sentence: The staff are exchanging ideas before the meeting.
examples.note: British English can use a plural verb to highlight individual staff members.

examples.sentence: Six weeks is enough time to finish the project.
examples.note: The six weeks are considered one time period.

commonMistakes.why: Trousers takes a plural verb even when only one pair is meant.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The news about the flight are disappointing.
commonMistakes.correct: The news about the flight is disappointing.
commonMistakes.why: News behaves as a singular, uncountable noun.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The police is checking the security cameras.
commonMistakes.correct: The police are checking the security cameras.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Four kilometres are too far for this short walk.
commonMistakes.correct: Four kilometres is too far for this short walk.
commonMistakes.why: The distance is judged as one total, so use is.

studyTips: Test agreement by finding the head noun: these scissors are, but this pair of scissors is.
Make a two-column list for tricky -s endings: school subjects and news are singular; police and people are plural.
With a collective noun, decide whether you mean the organisation as one unit or its members, and keep agreement consistent.

exercises.prompt: The safety goggles ___ on the shelf beside the helmets.
exercises.feedback: Goggles is a plural-only noun, so it takes are.

exercises.prompt: ___ one of the hardest subjects in the engineering programme.
exercises.feedback: The subject name physics is grammatically singular.

exercises.prompt: We identified four different ___ in the pond during the survey.
exercises.feedback: Species has the same spelling with singular and plural meanings.

exercises.prompt: The police ___ looking for the owner of the abandoned suitcase.
exercises.feedback: Police is plural in standard English and takes are looking.

exercises.prompt: After the hike, my boots were dry, but my trousers ___ still wet. (Write the past form of be.)
exercises.feedback: Trousers takes the plural form were.

exercises.prompt: I could not hear the announcement because the ___ was unclear. (Write the singular noun meaning information about recent events.)
exercises.feedback: News has an -s ending but takes singular was.

exercises.prompt: The students watched two documentary ___ about deep-sea animals. (Use the noun series.)
exercises.feedback: The plural of series is still series.

exercises.prompt: In this budget, thirty euros ___ enough for the bus tickets. (Complete with is or are; treat the amount as one total.)
exercises.feedback: A single amount of money takes singular agreement.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My new sunglasses is in the blue case.
acceptedAnswers: My new sunglasses are in the blue case.
exercises.feedback: Sunglasses is a plural-only noun, so use are.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Several peoples were waiting outside the theatre.
acceptedAnswers: Several people were waiting outside the theatre.
exercises.feedback: People is already the ordinary plural of person; do not add -s here.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The police has questioned both drivers.
acceptedAnswers: The police have questioned both drivers.
exercises.feedback: Police takes plural agreement, so the auxiliary is have.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Ten hours are too long for a single shift.
acceptedAnswers: Ten hours is too long for a single shift.
exercises.feedback: Ten hours describes one duration being evaluated, so singular is is natural.

speakingExercises.prompt: State the location of one set of glasses using these exact facts: my reading glasses; be; on the desk. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: My reading glasses are on the desk.
speakingExercises.feedback: Glasses takes plural are even when only one set is meant.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change only the incorrect verb and say the complete sentence: “Economics are my favourite subject.”
speakingExercises.feedback: Economics as a school subject takes a singular verb.

speakingExercises.prompt: A colleague asks whether the update is useful. Give one sentence beginning “The news” and ending “encouraging”.
speakingExercises.feedback: News is singular, so use is.

speakingExercises.prompt: Report this exact viewing history in one sentence: we; watch; two documentary series; last month. Use past simple.
acceptedAnswers: We watched two documentary series last month.
speakingExercises.feedback: Series is unchanged in the plural; two gives the number.

speakingExercises.prompt: The officers are checking witness statements. Explain what the police are doing in one complete sentence beginning “The police”. Use the present continuous and the exact words “checking witness statements”.
acceptedAnswers: The police are checking witness statements.
speakingExercises.feedback: Police is plural and takes are checking.

speakingExercises.prompt: In British English, treat the committee as one decision-making unit. Say this fact: the committee; have decided; to postpone the vote. Use singular agreement and one sentence.
acceptedAnswers: The committee has decided to postpone the vote.
speakingExercises.feedback: When the committee is viewed as one unit, has decided is appropriate.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say exactly two sentences using these facts: my headphones / be / new. This pair / be / comfortable. Use the present simple in both sentences.
acceptedAnswers: My headphones are new. This pair is comfortable.
speakingExercises.feedback: Headphones is plural; the head noun pair is singular.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a single judgement about one walking distance using the exact words: three kilometres / be / too far / before breakfast. Start with “Three kilometres”.
acceptedAnswers: Three kilometres is too far to walk before breakfast.
speakingExercises.feedback: The distance is considered as one amount, so use is.

listeningExercises.audioText: The update is reassuring: the news is good, although my protective glasses are damaged.
listeningExercises.feedback: The glasses are damaged; good describes the news, not the eyewear.

listeningExercises.audioText: We bought two pairs of binoculars for the wildlife volunteers, one for each team.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many sets of binoculars did they buy?
listeningExercises.feedback: Two pairs refers to two sets of binoculars.

listeningExercises.audioText: The police are checking the cameras outside the station.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word verb phrase immediately after “The police”.
listeningExercises.feedback: Police takes the plural present-continuous verb phrase are checking.

listeningExercises.audioText: The design team are comparing their proposals before the manager selects a single option.
listeningExercises.prompt: What are the team members doing before the decision?
listeningExercises.feedback: The plural team agreement highlights the members comparing their proposals.

listeningExercises.audioText: We watched two science series last weekend, but only one series covered space travel.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the programmes were about space travel?
listeningExercises.feedback: One series covered space travel; series stays the same in both numbers.

listeningExercises.audioText: Eight kilometres is the complete length of the charity route, not the distance from the car park.
choices: The drive from the car park.
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker calls it the complete length of the route.

listeningExercises.audioText: Physics is taught in the upstairs classroom on Wednesdays.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word verb phrase immediately after “Physics”.
listeningExercises.feedback: Physics is the singular subject of is taught.

listeningExercises.audioText: Several people are waiting outside the health centre for the doors to open.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three words immediately after “Several”.
listeningExercises.feedback: People is plural, and it takes are waiting.
